outcome_detail: $425,000 settlement unanimously approved by the Phoenix City Council on June 2, 2021. The city's internal investigation had substantiated the plaintiff's claim.
criminal_detail: Pena was fired in July 2020 and indicted by a grand jury on August 12, 2020, on seven felony counts (sexual assault and unlawful sexual conduct) involving three women. At his first trial in May 2022 a jury acquitted him on two counts and deadlocked on the remaining five; at an August 2022 retrial a second jury acquitted him on all remaining counts. Pena later sued the city and prosecutors over his termination and prosecution.
description: A woman sued the City of Phoenix in December 2020, alleging that then-Phoenix police officer Sean Pena sexually assaulted her on June 1, 2019, while she was in custody in the back of his patrol car. According to city officials, an internal investigation substantiated the claim, and the law department learned of similar allegations from other women. The Phoenix City Council unanimously approved a $425,000 settlement on June 2, 2021. Pena was fired in 2020 and criminally charged with offenses involving three women, but juries acquitted him on all counts across two trials in 2022.
notes: Filed before 2021; included because resolution occurred in window. Companion record rec-21b covers a second, separately filed suit by another accuser of Pena that the city settled for another $425,000 in November 2021.
